sanskrit: hiraṇyapuṣpī subhagā kūpaś cāyaṃ sumaṅgalaḥ | tāv enāṃ bhadrayā dhattām amṛtāv amṛte bhage ||
english: The golden-flowered plant is auspicious, and this well too is most propitious; let those two — both immortal — bestow upon her well-being with good fortune, within the immortal realm of Bhaga.

sanskrit: hiraṇyaṃ pṛḍvad dharitaṃ tat te aṅgeṣu rohatu | tenemām aśvinā nārīṃ bhagenābhi ṣiñcatam ||
english: That which is gold, abundant and yellow — may it grow upon your limbs. With that, O Aśvins, sprinkle this woman with the power of Bhaga.

sanskrit: yathā kūpam udahṛtas tṛṣyanto yanti kāminaḥ | evā tvā sarve devaraḥ patayo yantu kāminaḥ ||
english: Just as those who are thirsty and filled with desire come eagerly to a well that yields water, so may all your brothers-in-law and would-be husbands come to you with desire.

sanskrit: hiraṇyākṣi madhuvarṇe hiraṇyaparicartane | aṅko hiraṇyayas tava tenāsyai patim ā vaha ||
english: O plant golden-eyed, of honey-hued color, tended round with gold — your mark is of gold; with it bring a husband to this woman.

sanskrit: yadi vāsi tiro janaṃ yadi vā nadyas tiraḥ | iyaṃ tvā mahyam oṣadhir aṅkeneva ny ā nayāt ||
english: Whether you are beyond the people, or beyond the rivers — may this herb bring you to me as if with a hook, drawing you here.

sanskrit: punaḥ prāṇaṃ punar apānam asmai punar vyānam uta soma dhehi | ātmāyaṃ cakṣur ?udate samānas tam ū nu pāhi tam ū nu jinva jāgṛhi ||
english: Restore the in-breath, restore the out-breath, restore also the pervading breath to this man, O Soma. This self, this eye — the vital spirit rises together; do protect him now, do quicken him, awaken.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā rūpeṇa savitā savena- -ahar mitreṇa varuṇena rātrī | indro jyaiṣṭhyena brahmaṇāyaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ pūṣāsmai punar asuṃ dadhātu ||
english: Tvaṣṭṛ by his shaping power, Savitṛ by his impulsion — the day by Mitra and the night by Varuṇa; Indra by his supremacy, this one by sacred speech, Bṛhaspati and Pūṣan — may they restore life-breath to this man.

sanskrit: ya ādityā vasavo ye ca rudrā viśve devā aditir yā ca rātrī | yajño bhagaḥ savitā ye ca devā yamo 'smai punar asuṃ dadhātu ||
english: The Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the All-Gods, Aditi, and the Night; Yajña, Bhaga, Savitṛ, and whatever other gods there are — may Yama restore the life-breath to this man.

sanskrit: punas te rājā varuṇo dadātu somo rājāsum it te punar dāt | indro marudbhir aśvinā te bhiṣajyatām agnī rudro 'sum it te punar dāt ||
english: May King Varuṇa grant it to you again; may King Soma restore the life-breath to you. Let Indra with the Maruts, and the two Aśvins, heal you; may Agni and Rudra restore the life-breath to you.

sanskrit: punar dyaur devī punar antarikṣam agnir vātaḥ pavamāno bhiṣajyatu | grāhyāḥ pāśān nirṛtyāḥ pāśān mṛtyoḥ pāśād vāk tvā devī punar dadātu ||
english: May divine Heaven and the Atmosphere, Agni, Vāta, and Pavamāna heal you again. From the fetters of the Seizure, from the fetters of Nirṛti, from the fetters of Death — may the divine goddess Vāc restore you.

sanskrit: idaṃ cakṣur ṛtāvarī mā mā hāsīt purāyuṣaḥ | yad vāṃ tamo yad ripiśam apa vāṃ tan ni dadhmasi ||
english: O guardian of sacred order, may this eye of mine not abandon me before my full span of life. Whatever darkness there is in you both, whatever malignant film — that we blow away from you both.

sanskrit: yad andhiyaṃ yad algaṇaṃ yo 'rmo adhirohati | ayasmayas tad aṅkuśo akṣṇo 'rmam apa lumpatu ||
english: Whatever blindness there is, whatever dimness, whatever film creeps over the eye — may the iron hook strip away that film from the eye.

sanskrit: yam ahyājim ajayan nṛcakṣā yaṃ vā śyenaḥ śakunir yaṃ suparṇaḥ | yad āhuś cakṣur aditer anantaṃ somo nṛcakṣā mayi tad dadhātu ||
english: The sight that man-seeing Soma won in the contest with the serpent, or that which the hawk, the bird, the Suparṇa possesses — that which they call the boundless eye of Aditi, may man-seeing Soma place that in me.

sanskrit: yathā cakṣuḥ suparṇasya yathāśvasya yathā śunaḥ | evā me aśvinā cakṣuḥ kṛṇutaṃ puṣkarasrajā ||
english: As is the eye of the Suparṇa, as of the horse, as of the dog — even so, O Aśvins garlanded with lotuses, make my eye.

sanskrit: yasyāḥ suparṇaḥ prapatañ cakṣuṣā cakṣur ādade | tasyāḥ samudraje tava cakṣuṣā cakṣur ā dade ||
english: From her whose eye the Suparṇa took, seizing sight with sight as he swooped down — from her, O ocean-born one, I take your eye with sight.
